applicable_failures: The scan reported 1,199 files with hits and 144 matters, but only the matter list was printed, with no check that every matter folder was covered. The first call's output is truncated, so full coverage was never confirmed.

The second call grepped the scan output for a hand-picked list of 13 matters (1009-00004, 1022-00008, 1036-00005, etc.) and printed at most 240 lines via sed. The other ~131 hit matters were never examined, so the candidate set was narrowed from filtered output.

The scan keeps only snippets containing 2026 dates plus signing/closing terms, so matters that signed with a different phrasing or no snippet hit are invisible. This is a prefilter, yet the summary treats 144 matters as the candidate universe.

The shortlist leans on snippets that describe target or planned dates (for example the 1009-00004 target signing of Feb 15, 2026 and the 1036-00005 target closing), which are not evidence of actual signing.
critique.concerns: The scan was a snippet-level keyword filter. The agent then narrowed to a hand-picked matter list through grep and a 240-line cap. Coverage of all matter folders was not verified, and no signed-versus-closed status was established for any matter. The self-assessment of goal reached is overstated. The named candidates rest on target-date language, not executed documents.
critique.recommendation: Compare the matter folders in the store against the matters scanned, and rerun any that timed out or were skipped. Then work through all 144 hit matters systematically, not a hand-picked subset. For each, list its files and open the executed agreement and any closing or status document. Record signing date and closing status per matter.
